title: Amos Hochstein on the Iran war’s impact on energy: Oil prices are not reflecting reality
summary: Former energy adviser argues Iran still effectively controls the Strait of Hormuz, oil prices are held down by reserve releases and Washington headlines rather than fundamentals, and gasoline is high relative to crude.

assertions.quote: IRAN TOOK CONTROL OF THE STRAITS, RIGHT BY CLOSING THEM NOW.

verdicts.note: Depends on shipping data; a CNBC traffic analysis showed a three-month low in transits while the administration claims total control.

assertions.quote: THE MARKET IS TREATING THE SPR AS THOUGH THAT'S PRODUCTION. IT'S NOT PRODUCTION, IT'S NOT RENEWABLE, IT'S NOT SUSTAINABLE.

verdicts.note: A market call; reserve draws do add temporary supply, but whether the price is wrong cannot be settled from the data cited.

assertions.quote: GASOLINE SHOULD BE LOWER AT AN $81 OIL PRICE. BUT GASOLINE IS OVER $4.

verdicts.note: Historically $80 WTI maps to roughly $3.30-3.60 gasoline; refined-product tightness and wide crack spreads kept pump prices above that in 2026.

Regular gasoline minus the crude cost per gallon (WTI/42) was 2.04 in Sep 2026 (4.355 minus 97.31/42) and about 2.02-2.06 every month since June 2026, against 1.54-1.71 in Sep 2023, Sep 2024 and Sep 2025 and 2.20 at the Jun 2022 peak, so the retail margin over crude is roughly 0.35-0.50 per gallon above its recent norm; October crude is not yet in the file.

assertions.quote: THE CONSUMER PRICES ARE GOING TO GO UP MUCH HIGHER, MUCH FASTER.

verdicts.note: A conditional forecast about a renewed conflict.

assertions.quote: WE'RE HAVING A HARDER TIME RELEASING OUT OF THE SPR BECAUSE WHY THEY'RE LOWER SO THEY'RE CONSTRAINED.

verdicts.note: The SPR fell below 300 million barrels, its lowest since the 1980s, which constrains but does not end releases.
